User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the HealthAI application, linked to an external authentication system. This entity stores core user information without sensitive authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity. This typically corresponds to the user ID from the external authentication system (e.g., Firebase Auth).

email.description: The user's email address, obtained from the authentication system.

displayName.description: The user's display name, if available from the authentication system or set by the user.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user account information was last updated.

Prescription.title: Prescription
Prescription.description: Represents a digitized prescription document uploaded by a user, including its raw OCR output and processing status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Prescription entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who uploaded this prescription. (Relationship: User 1:N Prescription)

uploadDate.description: Date and time when the prescription document was uploaded.

documentUrl.description: URL to the stored original prescription document (image or PDF file).

rawOcrText.description: The raw text extracted from the prescription document using OCR (e.g., Google ML Kit).

isProcessed.description: Indicates whether the raw OCR text has been processed into structured medicine records.

notes.description: Any additional notes or comments the user adds about this prescription.

Medicine.title: Medicine
Medicine.description: Represents a single structured medication record managed by a user, potentially derived from a prescription or manually added.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Medicine entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who manages this medicine. (Relationship: User 1:N Medicine)

prescriptionId.description: Optional reference to the Prescription from which this medicine record was derived. (Relationship: Prescription 1:N Medicine)

name.description: The commercial or generic name of the medicine (e.g., 'Amoxicillin', 'Paracetamol').

dosage.description: The strength and quantity of the dose (e.g., '500 mg', '1 tablet').

form.description: The physical form of the medicine (e.g., 'tablet', 'capsule', 'liquid', 'inhaler').

frequency.description: How often the medicine should be taken (e.g., 'Once daily', 'Twice a day', 'Every 8 hours').

instructions.description: Specific instructions for taking the medicine (e.g., 'Take with food', 'Before bedtime', 'Do not crush').

startDate.description: The date when the user started or is supposed to start taking this medicine.

endDate.description: The date when the user is supposed to stop taking this medicine. Can be null for ongoing medications.

isActive.description: Indicates whether the medicine is currently active and being taken by the user.

aiInterpretation.description: AI-generated simple language explanation of the medicine's purpose, dosage, timing, food instructions, and precautions.

safetyNotes.description: AI-generated concise safety notes or warnings specific to this medication.

MedicationIntake.title: MedicationIntake
MedicationIntake.description: Records a specific scheduled dose of a medicine and its adherence status (taken, skipped, or missed).

id.description: Unique identifier for the MedicationIntake event.

medicineId.description: Reference to the Medicine associated with this intake. (Relationship: Medicine 1:N MedicationIntake)

scheduledTime.description: The date and time when the medicine dose was scheduled to be taken.

actualTakeTime.description: The date and time when the user marked the dose as taken. Null if not taken.

status.description: The adherence status of the dose (e.g., 'scheduled', 'taken', 'skipped', 'missed').

notes.description: Any user-provided notes regarding this specific intake (e.g., reason for skipping).

Reminder.title: Reminder
Reminder.description: Represents a notification reminder scheduled for a specific medication dose.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Reminder entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User for whom this reminder is created. (Relationship: User 1:N Reminder)

medicineId.description: Reference to the Medicine associated with this reminder. (Relationship: Medicine 1:N Reminder)

medicationIntakeId.description: Reference to the specific MedicationIntake event this reminder pertains to. (Relationship: MedicationIntake 1:N Reminder)

reminderTime.description: The exact date and time when the reminder notification should be delivered.

message.description: The content of the reminder message or notification.

isDelivered.description: Indicates whether the reminder notification has been successfully delivered.

deliveryAttemptedAt.description: Timestamp when the reminder delivery was attempted.

SafetyAlert.title: SafetyAlert
SafetyAlert.description: Stores safety alerts generated by the AI for drug interactions, duplicate therapies, or other risks.

id.description: Unique identifier for the SafetyAlert entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User to whom this alert pertains. (Relationship: User 1:N SafetyAlert)

medicineIds.description: References to the Medicine entities involved in this alert (e.g., interacting drugs). (Relationship: Medicine N:N SafetyAlert)

alertType.description: The category of the safety alert (e.g., 'Drug Interaction', 'Duplicate Therapy', 'Overdose Risk', 'Allergy Risk').

severity.description: The severity level of the alert (e.g., 'High', 'Medium', 'Low').

description.description: A detailed explanation of the safety concern.

recommendation.description: AI-generated recommendation or action plan based on the alert.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp when the safety alert was generated.

isAcknowledged.description: Indicates whether the user has acknowledged or dismissed this alert.

HealthcareProvider.title: HealthcareProvider
HealthcareProvider.description: Represents a healthcare professional (e.g., doctor, nurse) whose details can be manually stored or saved by the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the HealthcareProvider entity.

name.description: The full name of the healthcare provider.

specialty.description: The medical specialty of the provider (e.g., 'Cardiologist', 'General Practitioner').

contactNumber.description: The primary contact phone number for the provider.

email.description: The email address of the provider.

address.description: The physical address of the provider's clinic or office.

notes.description: General notes about the provider, potentially added by the user.

HealthcareFacility.title: HealthcareFacility
HealthcareFacility.description: Represents a healthcare facility (e.g., hospital, clinic, pharmacy) whose details can be manually stored or saved by the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the HealthcareFacility entity.

name.description: The name of the healthcare facility.

address.description: The full physical address of the facility.

contactNumber.description: The primary contact phone number for the facility.

website.description: The official website URL of the facility.

googlePlacesId.description: Optional ID from Google Places API, if the facility was discovered via the API.

latitude.description: The latitude coordinate of the facility's location.

longitude.description: The longitude coordinate of the facility's location.

notes.description: General notes about the facility, potentially added by the user.

UserPreferredProvider.title: UserPreferredProvider
UserPreferredProvider.description: An associative entity linking a User to a HealthcareProvider they have marked as preferred or saved.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserPreferredProvider entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who saved this provider. (Relationship: User 1:N UserPreferredProvider)

providerId.description: Reference to the HealthcareProvider entity that was saved. (Relationship: HealthcareProvider 1:N UserPreferredProvider)

savedAt.description: Timestamp when the provider was marked as preferred by the user.

userNotes.description: User-specific notes or context related to why this provider was saved.

UserPreferredFacility.title: UserPreferredFacility
UserPreferredFacility.description: An associative entity linking a User to a HealthcareFacility they have marked as preferred or saved.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserPreferredFacility entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who saved this facility. (Relationship: User 1:N UserPreferredFacility)

facilityId.description: Reference to the HealthcareFacility entity that was saved. (Relationship: HealthcareFacility 1:N UserPreferredFacility)

savedAt.description: Timestamp when the facility was marked as preferred by the user.

userNotes.description: User-specific notes or context related to why this facility was saved.

ChatSession.title: ChatSession
ChatSession.description: Represents a single conversation session between a user and the AI medication chat assistant.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ChatSession entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who initiated this chat session. (Relationship: User 1:N ChatSession)

startedAt.description: Timestamp when the chat session was initiated.

lastActivityAt.description: Timestamp of the last message exchanged in the session.

title.description: An optional AI-generated summary or title for the chat session.

ChatMessage.title: ChatMessage
ChatMessage.description: Represents an individual message exchanged within a ChatSession.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ChatMessage entity.

chatSessionId.description: Reference to the ChatSession this message belongs to. (Relationship: ChatSession 1:N ChatMessage)

content.description: The text content of the message.

sentAt.description: Timestamp when the message was sent.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure for the HealthAI application is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence, enabling robust and easily debuggable security rules. The core strategy revolves around segregating all user-specific and sensitive data into dedicated subcollections under a top-level `/users/{userId}` collection. This path-based ownership ensures that authorization rules can consistently check `request.auth.uid == userId` directly against the document's path or a denormalized `userId` field.

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
To achieve critical authorization independence, the following entities will have the `userId` field explicitly denormalized within their documents, even if it's implicitly available in the path: `Prescription`, `Medicine`, `MedicationIntake`, `Reminder`, `SafetyAlert`, `ChatSession`, `ChatMessage`. This prevents the need for costly and complex `get()` calls in security rules to check parent documents for ownership. For `ChatMessage`, `userId` will be copied from its parent `ChatSession` upon creation, ensuring each message document can be authorized independently. Similarly, for `UserPreferredProvider` and `UserPreferredFacility`, key display fields like `providerName`, `providerSpecialty`, `facilityName`, and `facilityAddress` (along with `userId`) are denormalized from their respective global `HealthcareProvider` and `HealthcareFacility` entities. This allows rules to authorize access based solely on the `UserPreferredProvider` or `UserPreferredFacility` document itself, without needing to `get()` the linked global entity, thereby maintaining atomic operations and rule simplicity.

**QAPs (Secure List Operations):**
The structural segregation is fundamental for Query-Aware Permissions (QAPs). By placing all user-specific data under `/users/{userId}/...`, `list` operations (queries) can be secured with rules such as `allow list: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. This ensures that a user can only query and retrieve their own data. For example, a query to `/users/{userId}/prescriptions` will automatically be filtered by the `userId` in the path, and the rule `allow list: if request.auth.uid == userId;` will prevent unauthorized access or listing of other users' prescriptions. This design effectively makes rules not act as filters but as enforcers of pre-filtered queries.

**Structural Segregation & Access Modeling:**
*   **Private Data:** All personal health records (Prescriptions, Medicines, MedicationIntakes, Reminders, SafetyAlerts) are strictly path-based and user-owned, located under `/users/{userId}/`. This guarantees a homogeneous security posture for all documents within these collections – only the owner can read/write them.
*   **Chat Data:** Chat sessions (`ChatSession`) and messages (`ChatMessage`) are also privately owned, nested under the user's path, further reinforcing private data access.
*   **Global vs. User-Saved Data:** `HealthcareProvider` and `HealthcareFacility` are structured as global, read-only collections. These are intended for system-managed lookups (e.g., from Google Places API or admin input). Users then 'save' or 'prefer' these via `UserPreferredProvider` and `UserPreferredFacility` collections, which are user-owned. This separation, combined with denormalization in the 'preferred' entities, maintains authorization independence while allowing for a global catalog.

This architecture prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by embedding authorization context directly within documents and utilizing clear, hierarchical paths for user-owned data, minimizing `get()` calls, and simplifying Firestore security rules.
